symbols.name: Golden Calf
symbols.explanation: The Israelites made a golden calf to worship, turning away from God. This symbol represents idolatry and the danger of placing anything above God in our lives.

symbols.name: Roman Gold Coin
symbols.explanation: Jesus taught, 'You cannot serve both God and money.' Wealth becomes an idol when we love and trust in it, rather than in God who provides all things.

symbols.name: Sun Worship
symbols.explanation: God specifically commanded the Israelites not to worship the sun, moon, or stars. This represents the error of worshiping created things rather than the Creator.

symbols.name: Triple Spiral Wiccan
symbols.explanation: This symbol is associated with modern witchcraft (Wicca), which the Bible forbids. Scripture warns against witchcraft, sorcery, and seeking spiritual power or guidance from any source other than the one true God.

symbols.name: Serpent Idol
symbols.explanation: Even a God-ordained object, like the bronze serpent Moses made, can become an idol if people worship it. King Hezekiah destroyed it because the Israelites began burning incense to it, which is an act of worship reserved for God alone.

symbols.name: Aries Zodiac Sign
symbols.explanation: Astrology and fortune-telling are forbidden because they seek guidance from created things (stars) instead of the Creator. The Bible mocks those who trust in stargazers, saying they cannot save themselves, let alone others.

symbols.name: Amulet
symbols.explanation: Amulets and magic charms are condemned in the Bible. They represent a false trust in objects for protection or power, which should only come from God.

symbols.name: Ankh
symbols.explanation: The ankh is an ancient Egyptian symbol for 'life.' This can be a form of idolatry when it represents a source of life apart from God. Jesus Christ is the only way to eternal life.

symbols.name: Aztec Temple
symbols.explanation: Pagan temples were often built on 'high places' for the worship of false gods, an act Solomon himself fell into. The Bible teaches that the true God does not dwell in temples made by human hands.

symbols.name: Celtic Rune
symbols.explanation: Runes are used for divination and sorcery, practices the Bible strictly forbids. We are commanded not to consult mediums or spirits, but to seek wisdom from God alone.

symbols.name: Celtic Tree of Life
symbols.explanation: This symbol can represent nature worship, similar to the pagan custom of cutting a tree from the forest and decorating it. The Bible teaches there is only one mediator between God and men, Jesus Christ, not a mystical tree.

symbols.name: Chakana
symbols.explanation: This symbol represents a non-biblical worldview and cosmology. The Bible warns us not to be taken captive by human tradition and the basic principles of this world, rather than on Christ. We are to have no other gods before the Lord.

symbols.name: Confucianism Symbol
symbols.explanation: Confucianism is a philosophy that emphasizes human ethics and wisdom. While it may seem good, it is a path that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death, because it does not acknowledge Jesus as the only way to the Father.

symbols.name: Ganesh
symbols.explanation: Ganesh is a Hindu deity, an idol made by human hands. The Bible teaches that an idol is nothing at all, and that those who make them will be put to shame. We know there is no God but one.

symbols.name: Hecates Wheel
symbols.explanation: This is a symbol used in modern witchcraft to represent a goddess. The Bible is clear that rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and that sorcerers will have their place in the lake of fire.

symbols.name: Hindu Om Symbol
symbols.explanation: The Om symbol represents a universal sound or vibration in Hinduism. This contradicts the Bible, which says 'In the beginning was the Word (Jesus),' and that through Him all things were made and are held together.

symbols.name: Celtic Knot
symbols.explanation: This symbol can represent endlessness or eternity apart from Heaven (with God) and Hell (apart from God). The Bible teaches that eternal life is not an abstract concept, but is found in knowing the one true God and Jesus Christ whom He sent.

symbols.name: Celtic Moon
symbols.explanation: Worshiping the moon is a form of idolatry explicitly forbidden by God. The Bible teaches that our understanding of nature comes from God the Creator of time, space, and everything in it.

symbols.name: Mystical Eye
symbols.explanation: This symbol represents a promise of secret knowledge or enlightenment, echoing the Satan's lie in the garden that 'your eyes will be opened.' It is a deception, as Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light but in reality is the father of lies.

symbols.name: Pagan Cross
symbols.explanation: This symbol, often with equal arms, represents a pre-Christian, pagan concept. Mixing it with Christian meaning is syncretism. The Bible warns not to be yoked with unbelievers and that there is no harmony between Christ and Belial (a term for the devil).

symbols.name: Pagan Cross in Circle
symbols.explanation: This symbol, often called a 'sun cross,' combines a pagan symbol with the cross. This represents a distortion of the gospel, presenting 'another Jesus' or a 'different gospel,' which the Apostle Paul warns against.

symbols.name: Paganism Symbol
symbols.explanation: Paganism involves the worship of false gods, idols, and created things. The Bible says that what pagans sacrifice they offer to demons and not to God.

symbols.name: Ramadan Symbol
symbols.explanation: The crescent and star are symbols of Islam, a religion that denies that Jesus is the Son of God. The Bible teaches that Jesus is the only way to the Father and warns that even if an angel from heaven preaches another gospel, he is to be accursed.

symbols.name: Sikhism
symbols.explanation: The Khanda is the symbol of Sikhism, a religion that does not recognize Jesus Christ as the only Son of God and savior. The Bible is clear that salvation is found in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to mankind by which we must be saved.

symbols.name: Swastika Symbol
symbols.explanation: Though an ancient symbol, the swastika is now inseparable from the evil of Nazism, which was hostile to Christianity, and attempted to wipe entire people groups from the face of the earth using macro-evolution as justification for racism. The Bible says there is only one race, the human race; we all come from Adam and Eve via Noah and his Family.

symbols.name: Tao Yin Yang
symbols.explanation: The Yin-Yang represents a dualistic balance of good and evil. The Bible teaches that God is sovereign over both light and darkness, and asks, 'What fellowship has light with darkness?'

symbols.name: Tiki Idol
symbols.explanation: Tiki idols are man-made images worshiped as gods. The Bible says such idols are silver and gold, the work of human hands. They have mouths, but do not speak; eyes, but do not see. Those who make them become like them.

symbols.name: Triquetra Symbol
symbols.explanation: This symbol, used in ancient paganism and modern witchcraft, represents concepts outside of biblical truth. It is a hollow and deceptive philosophy, which depends on human tradition and the elemental spiritual forces of this world rather than on Christ.

symbols.name: Valknut Symbol
symbols.explanation: This Norse pagan symbol is associated with death and the god Odin. This is idolatry. The Bible teaches that it is appointed for man to die once, and after that comes judgment, and that Jesus is the resurrection and the life.

symbols.name: Cross
symbols.explanation: The cross represents Jesus’ sacrifice for our sins. It is a symbol of hope and redemption.

symbols.name: Empty Tomb
symbols.explanation: The empty tomb signifies Jesus’ resurrection, the cornerstone of Christian faith.

symbols.name: Dove
symbols.explanation: The dove represents the Holy Spirit, who descended upon Jesus at His baptism.

symbols.name: Heart
symbols.explanation: The heart symbolizes God’s love for us and our love for Him.

symbols.name: Angel
symbols.explanation: Angels are messengers of God, serving and protecting His people.

symbols.name: Alpha & Omega
symbols.explanation: Alpha and Omega represent the beginning and the end, signifying God’s eternal nature.

symbols.name: Fish (Ichthys)
symbols.explanation: The fish symbol represents Jesus and His followers, who are called to be 'fishers of men'.

symbols.name: Noah’s Ark
symbols.explanation: Noah’s Ark represents God’s salvation and covenant with humanity.

symbols.name: Bread
symbols.explanation: Bread symbolizes Jesus as the Bread of Life, sustaining us spiritually.

symbols.name: Wine
symbols.explanation: Wine represents the blood of Christ, shed for our sins.

symbols.name: Shepherd
symbols.explanation: The shepherd symbolizes Jesus as the Good Shepherd, who cares for His flock.

symbols.name: Palm Leaf
symbols.explanation: The palm leaf symbolizes victory and triumph, as seen during Jesus’ triumphal entry into Jerusalem.

symbols.name: Star of Bethlehem
symbols.explanation: The Star of Bethlehem guided the wise men to Jesus’ birthplace, symbolizing divine guidance.

symbols.name: Bible
symbols.explanation: The Bible is the inspired Word of God, providing guidance and truth for believers.

symbols.name: Candle
symbols.explanation: The candle symbolizes Jesus as the Light of the world, illuminating our path.

symbols.name: Chalice
symbols.explanation: The chalice represents the blood of Christ, shed for our sins during communion.

symbols.name: Lion of Judah
symbols.explanation: The lion symbolizes Jesus as the Lion of Judah, representing His power and authority.

symbols.name: Praying Hands
symbols.explanation: Praying hands symbolize the importance of prayer in a believer’s life.

symbols.name: Rainbow
symbols.explanation: The rainbow symbolizes God’s covenant with Noah, representing His promise never to flood the earth again.

symbols.name: Star of David
symbols.explanation: The Star of David symbolizes the Jewish faith and God’s covenant with His people.

symbols.name: Manger
symbols.explanation: The manger represents Jesus’ humble birth, signifying His incarnation.

symbols.name: Vine
symbols.explanation: Jesus is the true vine, and we are the branches, symbolizing our connection to Him.

symbols.name: Wheat
symbols.explanation: Wheat symbolizes the harvest of souls, representing the growth of God’s kingdom.

symbols.name: Sling-Shot
symbols.explanation: David used a sling and a stone to defeat Goliath, symbolizing faith and courage.

symbols.name: Star
symbols.explanation: The star guided three wise men to Jesus, symbolizing divine guidance.

symbols.name: Temple of Jerusalem
symbols.explanation: The Temple of Jerusalem represents God’s dwelling place among His people, symbolizing worship and sacrifice.

symbols.name: Pentagram
symbols.explanation: The Pentagram is often associated with modern paganism and witchcraft, representing the elements. It can lead to idolatry if it replaces the worship of the true God.

symbols.name: Crown of Thorns
symbols.explanation: The crown of thorns symbolizes Jesus’ suffering and kingship, worn during His crucifixion.

symbols.name: Ten Commandments
symbols.explanation: The Ten Commandments represent God’s moral law given to Moses for His people.

symbols.name: Anchor
symbols.explanation: The anchor symbolizes hope in Christ, which is a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.

symbols.name: Lily
symbols.explanation: The lily symbolizes purity and the resurrection of Jesus, often associated with Easter.
